overview: From 2026-10-11 to 2026-10-18, ethereum-optimism/optimism had 20 new PRs (19 merged), 4 new issues, and 30 active contributors.

topIssues.title: op-reth: delay proofs ExEx acknowledgements until indexing completes
topIssues.author: joshklop
topIssues.body:
## Description

The proofs-history ExEx can emit `FinishedHeight` immediately after scheduling asynchronous catch-up with `sync_to`, before the proof engine has indexed that height. This can let reth prune the replay data that catch-up still needs.

When catch-up reaches a block whose parent state is not available yet, `StateForHashNotFound` is currently converted to success without advancing the proof tip. The engine resets its retry backoff on that apparent success and can retry the same block in a tight loop.

## Expected behavior

- Emit `FinishedHeight` only for heights the proof engine has actually indexed.
- Treat unavailable parent state as a no-progress retry and apply exponential backoff.
- Resume and acknowledge progress once the state becomes available.

## Context

Found while reviewing the reth v2.6.0 bump: https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/23046#discussion_r4135197920

topIssues.title: op-reth: include pending block logs in eth_getLogs ranges
topIssues.author: joshklop
topIssues.body:
`eth_getLogs` ranges whose upper bound is `pending` currently resolve that bound to the canonical head unless the range also starts at `pending`. Requests such as `latest..pending` therefore return successfully while omitting logs from the local pending block.

This is not flashblock-specific: op-reth omits sequencer flashblock logs, while upstream Reth omits logs from its locally built pending block when pending-block construction is enabled.

The focused fix is in draft PR #23103, stacked on the Reth update in #23046. Original review finding: https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/23046#discussion_r4135197967

topIssues.title: op-supernode: Full rewind deletes backfilled logs and invalidates valid blocks
topIssues.author: ajsutton
topIssues.body:
**Claude:** I found this while I reviewed ethereum-optimism/optimism#22846.

A full rewind deletes every chain's logsDB, including the cold-start backfill. The backfill is the history the node needs to verify the timestamps it is about to replay. After the delete, the node invalidates valid blocks.

## Event sequence

1. `buildRewindPlan` returns a plan with a nil `TargetHeads` when `lastTS <= firstVerifiableTimestamp` (`interop.go:953-961`).
2. `applyRewindPlan` then calls `db.Clear()` on every chain (`interop.go:1065-1070`).
3. `clearLocked` deletes the whole range and resets `firstBlock` to 0 (`db.go:474-484`).
4. Verification resumes at the first verifiable timestamp with an empty logsDB.
5. `verifyExecutingMessage` calls `Contains` for an initiating message that the backfill held (`algo.go:229-231`).
6. `Contains` returns `interop.ErrFuture` because `hasBlocks` is false (`db.go:287-289`).
7. `verifyInteropMessages` treats the error as an invalid executing message (`algo.go:129-141`).
8. The round applies `DecisionInvalidate` and replaces a valid block.

## Why the delete is wrong

The logsDB holds history below `firstVerifiableTimestamp` on purpose. `runColdStartBackfill` seals one message expiry window of history before the first verified timestamp (`log_backfill.go:100-166`). A rewind of the verified state to that timestamp does not make the backfill invalid. It is exactly the history the node needs to verify that timestamp again.

## Why the node does not recover

Cold start runs once, from `Start` (`interop.go:333`). `waitingForSync` never returns to true, so no backfill re-runs in process.

A restart repairs the node only if the verifiedDB also emptied. If any commit survives, `tryInitFromVerifiedDB` resumes and skips backfill (`interop.go:342-350`).

## Reachability

The window is narrow. A rewind removes one timestamp per round.

`progressInterop` calls `buildRewindPlan(*obs.LastVerifiedTS)` (`interop.go:736`). `observeRound` sets `LastVerifiedTS` from `verifiedDB.LastTimestamp()` (`interop.go:600-603`). So the plan always targets the last verified timestamp, not a reorg depth. The loop then re-checks `SameL1Chain` on the new last entry (`interop.go:635-643`) and repeats.

The verifiedDB has no pruning. `firstTimestamp` moves only in `Rewind`, and only downward or to empty (`verified_db.go:254-290`). So `first` stays at the first round the node ever verified, for the life of the data directory.

To reach `lastTS <= first`, the node must walk its verified DB back to the single first entry. The L1 reorg must invalidate the L1 inclusion of every verified timestamp. In practice the reorg depth must exceed the age of the verified DB. That gives two reachable cases:

1. A young verified DB. A node that cold-started minutes ago holds a recent `L1Inclusion` on its first entry. An ordinary one or two block L1 reorg reaches past it. If the node has verified exactly one timestamp, `last == first` and any L1 inconsistency triggers the clear at once.
2. After an operator wipes the data directory, which is the documented recovery path. That returns the node to case 1.

A mature node is effectively immune. The reorg would have to be deeper than the whole run.

A rewind to the interop activation timestamp is harmless. `runColdStartBackfill` clamps `commonStart` to `activationTimestamp` (`log_backfill.go:122`), so nothing is retained below activation, and a message cannot reference a pre-activation block anyway.

The damaging case is a node that cold-starts long after activation. `advanceColdStartInit` sets `verificationStartTimestamp` to `max(activation, max_c firstSafeHeadTS)` (`log_backfill.go:31-38`). The backfill below that point is real data, and the clear destroys it.

## Expected behavior

Truncate the logsDB to the last block that backfill sealed, instead of a full delete. Keep every block below `firstVerifiableTimestamp`. Clear the database only when the rewind reaches the interop activation timestamp.

In process, this is sufficient. After the verifiedDB empties, `observeRound` reads `firstVerifiableTimestamp`, which falls back to the unchanged `verificationStartTimestamp` (`interop.go:235-245`). So verification resumes at the same point that backfill ended.

Re-run backfill if the resume point can ever move later than the backfill end. `verifyCanAddTimestamp` rejects a gap larger than one block time (`logdb.go:193-198`), so a later resume point would wedge the seal path.

## Related

- ethereum-optimism/optimism#20627 added `reconcileLogsDBTail` and the backfill-path clear.
- ethereum-optimism/optimism#19287 introduced the L1 reorg rewind handling.
- ethereum-optimism/optimism#22846 covers storage errors that cause invalidation. This issue is a separate cause of the same outcome.

topIssues.title: op-challenger: support ZK dispute games in CLI commands
topIssues.author: pauldowman
topIssues.body:
Some op-challenger CLI commands do not yet support ZK games.

| Command | Status | Observed |
|---|---|---|
| `list-games` | works | lists game type 10 |
| `move --attack` | works | attaches `challengerBond()` |
| `list-claims` | fails | `unsupported game type: zk` |
| `list-credits` | fails | `unsupported game type: zk` |
| `game-proposal-outputs` | fails | `unsupported game type: zk` |
| `resolve` | fails | `unsupported game type: zk` |
| `resolve-claim` | fails | `unsupported game type: zk` |
| `create-game` | builds an invalid tx | reverts `BadExtraData()` |
| `run-trace` | accepts `zk`, cannot run it | no executor for the type |

## Root cause

`list-claims`, `list-credits`, `game-proposal-outputs`, `resolve` and `resolve-claim` all construct via `NewFaultDisputeGameContract` (`faultdisputegame.go:84`), which has no ZK case. The generic `NewDisputeGameContract` (`disputegame.go:52`) does — that is why `move` works.

## In scope

**`resolve`** — switch `resolve.go:15` to `DisputeGameContract` / `NewDisputeGameContract`, as `move.go:90` does. `ResolveTx()` is already on that interface.

**`list-credits`** — `GetBalanceAndDelay` and `GetWithdrawals` are already on `ZKDisputeGameContract` (`zkdisputegame.go:79-81`). Only the recipient set differs: challenger, prover and game creator instead of the claim tree.

**`game-proposal-outputs`** — needs `--superroot-rpc` / `superroot_atTimestamp`, because `L2SequenceNum` is a super-root timestamp, not a block number. **Already broken for `super-cannon-kona` and `super-permissioned`** for the same reason: they construct fine, then feed a timestamp to `OutputAtBlock` (`game_proposal_outputs.go:174`, `superfaultdisputegame.go:63`). That file has no super-game test coverage. The logic exists in `game/zk/actor.go`'s `SuperRootProvider`.

**`create-game`** — needed by the `op-challenger-invalid-proposal` CronJob (`ethereum-optimism/k8s`, every 12h). `createGameParams` (`gamefactory.go:313`) has no ZK case; ZK `extraData` is a 4-byte `parentIndex` plus a `SuperRootProof` (`ZKDisputeGame.sol:189-205`). Reuse the existing `encodeSuperRootProof` and add `--parent-index` defaulting to `uint32.max`, which anchors to the `AnchorStateRegistry` root and keeps the cron invocation unchanged. Note `initBonds(10)` is non-zero (0.021 ETH on zk-proofs-1) and is forfeited on each invalid proposal.

**ZK game state** — nothing exposes `claimData()` (proposal status, challenger, prover, deadline), which is what confirms a proof landed after a challenge. Needs a ZK branch in `list-claims` or a new subcommand.

**`list-games`** (cosmetic) — prints `Claims 0`, because `GetClaimCount` is only called for `FaultDisputeGameContract` (`list_games.go:134`).

`credits.go`, `resolve.go`, `resolve_claim.go` and `create_game.go` have no test files; follow the stub-RPC pattern in `move_test.go`.

## Out of scope

**`resolve-claim`** — ZK games have no `resolveClaim`. Improve the error message only.

**`run-trace`** — ZK has no VM trace. The bug is that `--run zk/...` is accepted: `PlayableGameTypes` (`game_type.go:43`) backs the parser, but `serverExecutorForGameType` (`runner/factory.go:61`) has no case for it — same for `alphabet` and `fast`. Add a separate trace-types list; `PlayableGameTypes` must keep ZK, since it also backs `--game-type`, config validation and the monitor.

topIssues.title: kona-interop: the proof cost of message validation grows as executing messages × initiating-block receipts
topIssues.author: Inphi
topIssues.body:
## Summary

For each executing message, `MessageGraph` walks to the initiating block's header and decodes all of that block's receipts. Nothing is cached, and identical messages are not deduplicated. `CrossL2Inbox.validateMessage` costs about 3.5k gas after the first call, so one transaction can emit about 11k messages that all point to one log in a block with large receipts.

## Measurements

SP1 executor, real guest ELF:

| Receipts | Messages | Cycles |
|---|---|---|
| 64 | 1 | 7.0M |
| 512 | 64 | 443M |
| 2048 | 256 | 6.94B |

The rate is about 13k cycles for each (message × receipt). An attack with about 11k messages against about 1 MB of receipts is about 4e11 cycles for one timestamp. One timestamp cannot be split across consolidation proofs.

## Where

- `rust/kona/crates/protocol/interop/src/graph.rs:198-211`: one header walk and one receipts decode for each message.
- `rust/kona/crates/proof/proof-interop/src/provider.rs:106-132`: a full receipts decode, with no cache.

## Impact

Liveness in interop clusters. For a few dollars of L2 gas, an attacker can make the proof for one timestamp too expensive to finish in `maxProveDuration`. The attacker then challenges each honest game that covers that timestamp and takes the bonds. The FPVM uses the same algorithm, but it has no prove deadline.

## Fix

1. Cache headers by number and decoded receipts by block hash, across messages and across consolidation iterations.
2. Validate each distinct identifier once.
3. Index logs so that each lookup costs a fixed amount, not a full walk.

topPRs.title: Add Lean proof of the super-aggregation coverage checks
topPRs.author: Inphi
topPRs.body:
Adds a Lean proof that `SuperAggregationInputs::validate` only accepts aggregations whose child outputs form one contiguous chain of super roots from the starting root to the root claim, with one range-derived block per chain and one consolidation step at every timestamp in between.

The Rust is extracted with Charon and Aeneas into `rust/kona/sp1/verification`. The main theorem is `KonaSp1.aggregation_sound`. It assumes child-proof soundness and `l2_sequence_number < u64::MAX`; the README lists the full trust base. `#print axioms` shows only Lean's standard axioms and the opaque super-root hash.

The `super_root.rs` change is only to suit the extractor: loops that returned early from nested or post-`?` positions move into private helpers, with the same accepted inputs and error order. A new test covers a chain-ID mismatch in a later timestamp block, the one loop that was rewritten rather than moved.

CI does not build the Lean project yet. `scripts/extract.sh` regenerates the generated files and `lake build` checks the proofs.

topPRs.title: kona-sp1: accelerate EIP-2537 BLS12-381 precompiles
topPRs.author: wwared
topPRs.body:
The kona-sp1 guest ran the EIP-2537 precompiles (0x0b–0x11) on revm's software arkworks backend, so any block that used them was expensive to prove. `CustomCrypto` now runs all seven on `sp1_bls12_381`, which uses SP1's field, point and bigint syscalls. In SP1's executor that is 5–26× fewer cycles per op (pairing 9.4×, G1 MSM 7.2×, G2 MSM 6.2×). Cycle counts overstate the proving saving, since syscalls cost more trace area; the one op measured in prover gas, a single-term G1 MSM, costs 3.6× less.

There is no behaviour change for chains or operators. The new backend must match arkworks bit for bit, including which `PrecompileHalt` wins when an input is invalid in several ways, because any divergence would make the proof disagree with the chain.

Closes https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/proofs-team/issues/11

**Pieces**
- `crates/client/src/precompiles/bls12_381.rs`: the backend. It decodes and encodes EIP-2537 bytes itself, because `sp1_bls12_381`'s serializers use ZCash flag bits. The module doc lists the APIs it must not use and the zkVM hint paths it relies on.
- `crates/bls12-381-check` (test-only): a vendored copy of revm's arkworks backend as the oracle, and a deterministic 1340-case corpus (torsion and off-subgroup points, non-canonical encodings, error precedence, MSM and pairing inputs at the Jovian and Isthmus caps). Host tests compare `CustomCrypto` with arkworks and blst and run the official EIP-2537 vectors.
- `programs/tests/bls12-381-check` (test-only guest) and `examples/zkvm_check.rs`: run the corpus through `CustomCrypto` and in-guest arkworks inside SP1's executor, the only place `sp1_bls12_381`'s syscall and hint paths run, and print per-op cycles (`just check-bls12-381-zkvm`).
- `.circleci/continue/rust-e2e.yml`: a nightly `sp1-bls12-381-zkvm-check` job that runs that check (executor only; proving the corpus nightly is too costly).

**Review focus**
- Error precedence: MSM stops at the first error and validates each point before dropping a zero-scalar term; pairing skips identity pairs by their raw bytes, as revm does.
- Malicious-prover guards: the `g2_to_affine` assert and the `read_fp` pre-check only fire on a forged hint, so no test exercises them. Re-audit the module doc's hint list whenever `sp1_bls12_381` changes.
- u = 0 in `map_fp2_to_g2`: `sp1_bls12_381`'s G2 map (inherited from zkcrypto `bls12_381`) returns an off-curve point there, so that input returns the reference output directly. Not reported upstream yet.
- The nightly job can't run on this PR; its first run is the first nightly on `develop`, and a failure pages @proofs-team.

**Design choices**
- MSMs with fewer than four terms use per-term multiplication, which is cheaper than the bucket method's fixed per-window cost. A G1-only affine point-syscall loop would cut 1–3-term G1 MSMs another 4.3× in prover gas; rejected as extra hand-written code for a rare op.
- The new job restores the toolchain cache twice to stay simple. The G1 map keeps its isogeny-kernel guard: the output is the same without it, but it keeps `clear_h` off a degenerate point.

topPRs.title: op-interop-mon: verify interop message expiries and ETH bridge refunds
topPRs.author: karlfloersch
topPRs.body:
op-interop-mon now checks the two safety rules of interop message expiry from chain data:

1. A destination never relays a message that its source marked expired.
2. Every SuperchainETHBridge burn is matched by at most one mint.

**What it reads.** The monitor already reads each chain's L2 receipts. Its finders now also pass every `MessageExpired` and `RefundETH` event to a new `ExpiryChecker`. The checker then reads the source and destination chains' logs and storage. It never relies on a contract call succeeding.

**What it produces.**

- `expiry_checks_total{chain_id,check,result}`
- `expiry_violations_total{chain_id,check,reason}`: the counter alerting should page on.
- `expiry_last_verified_block{chain_id}`
- `eth_in_flight` and `eth_in_flight_timestamp`

It also logs an error for each violation, with the message hash and the transaction.

**Who consumes it.** On-call alerting and dashboards, the same as the existing op-interop-mon metrics.

This PR follows the "Interop Message Expiry and Refund Monitoring" design doc. It covers the checks that enforce the safety rules. More monitoring will follow.

## Checks

- **Check 1, a relay after an expiry.** The existing window check already covers this. A message expires only once it has gone unrelayed for longer than the 8-day expiry period. Any later relay is therefore past the 7-day window, so the updater marks it `expired`. With `--supernode-endpoints` set, such a relay also counts in `cross_safety_violations_total` once it reaches cross-safe. A new updater test pins this case.
- **Check 2, expiry.** For each `MessageExpired(messageHash, undeliveredAt)` on source A:
  - a. `sentMessageTimestamps[H]` on A is nonzero.
  - b. A `SentMessage` in A's block at that time rebuilds to H. The hash is rebuilt in Go and tested against vectors from `cast`.
  - c. `undeliveredAt` is greater than `sentAt + expiryPeriod`, and not later than the block that expired the message.
  - d. Destination B has no `RelayedMessage(source=A, …, H)` within the window.
  - e. `successfulMessages[H]` is false on B at its head.
  - f. B's block at `undeliveredAt` contains `UndeliveredMessageExported(H, A, …, undeliveredAt)`.
- **Check 3, refund.** For each `RefundETH(from, amount, H)`:
  - H is expired.
  - The `SentMessage` for H is a bridge-to-bridge `relayETH(from, to, amount)`, with the same sender and amount as the refund.
  - The send transaction emitted the matching `SendETH` and an `ETHLiquidity` `LiquidityBurned` of the amount.
  - There is exactly one `RefundETH` for H between the send and this refund.
- **Check 4, ETH conservation.** Every 12 seconds, at one L2 timestamp across the chains:
  - Every `LiquidityBurned` is paired with a `SendETH` of the same amount in the same transaction.
  - Every `LiquidityMinted` is paired with a `RelayETH` or `RefundETH` of the same amount in the same transaction.
  - Each chain's ETHLiquidity figure, `balance - baseline - sum(LiquidityFunded)`, is compared with its bridge events (`SendETH - RelayETH - RefundETH`).
  - The cluster's ETH in flight is never negative.
  - The checker keeps only running sums, not lists of events.

Events are checked once their block is at or below `--expiry-check-head`, which is `finalized` by default and can be set to `safe`. Refunds are checked before expiries. An event whose block was reorged out is dropped. The conservation check starts over if a block it already counted is reorged out.

## Deviations from the doc

- **Check 4 tests equality, not only "never negative".** A per-chain mint smaller than the ETH in flight would hide inside the cluster total, so each chain is also checked against its own bridge events. The balance may exceed the events, but that excess must never shrink.
  - ETH forced into ETHLiquidity raises the balance without an event. That happens through a self-destruct, or through `relayETH` to ETHLiquidity itself. Anyone can do it.
  - Strict equality would therefore page on an attacker's 1 wei. Requiring the excess never to shrink still catches any ETH that leaves without an event, including after a forced send.
  - A double mint whose events look legitimate passes check 4: the same message both relayed and refunded. Checks 2 and 3, together with the window check, catch it. The code comment on the tripwire says so.
- **Head.** The doc does not choose one. The checks read only up to `finalized` by default, so a reorg cannot produce a false violation.
- **`sentAt == 0` on a `MessageExpired`** is reported as the violation `unknown_message`. `expireMessage` reverts for such messages, including those sent before send times were recorded.
- **Baseline for chains that activated interop by upgrade** (one of the doc's open questions). `--eth-liquidity-baseline-blocks <chain>=<block>` sets the baseline; it defaults to genesis. The L2 RPCs must serve state back to that block.
- **Check 3 checks two more things.** It also requires the ETHLiquidity burn, not only the `SendETH`, and it bounds the duplicate-refund query to the range from the send to the refund.
- **Doc errors.**
  - "relayUndeliveredMessage and refundETH don't check the pause" is wrong for `relayUndeliveredMessage`, which reverts with `L1CrossDomainMessenger_Paused`. `refundETH` does not check the pause.
  - `MessageExpired` carries no destination; the checks get it from the decoded `SentMessage`.
  - `UndeliveredMessageExported` also carries `sourceMessenger`, which this PR does not check. That needs the L1 addresses from step 2g.
  - Every other event, function and storage name in the doc matches the contracts.

## Tests

- **Unit tests.** They run against an in-memory chain and cover:
  - valid expiry, refund and conservation flows;
  - an expiry with no export, or an export for another source;
  - a relay within the window, and a relay after the expiry;
  - a hash mismatch, a message never sent, an early expiry, a fact from the future, an unmonitored destination, and waiting for the export to be final;
  - a refund with no expiry, a second refund, a refund to another sender or of another amount, a send that burned nothing, and a refund of a non-bridge message;
  - a send both refunded and relayed (negative in flight), a mint with no event, unpaired mints and burns, top-ups and forced ETH, forced ETH followed by an outflow, same-timestamp reads, a baseline block, catch-up over several checks, and a reorg below the conservation check's progress;
  - refund-first ordering, reorged events, and holding events until their block is final.
- **Acceptance test.** `TestUnrelayedMessageExpiresAndIsRefunded` now attaches op-interop-mon to both chains, reading finalized heads. It requires that the monitor checks the expiry and the refund as valid, checks conservation past the refund with nothing left in flight, and finds no violation.

## Not covered, and why

These are left out to keep this PR small and reviewable. Each is a follow-up:

- **Step 2g, linking the L1 legs.** This needs an L1 reader, plus each chain's L1 messenger and portal addresses. With those, the remaining steps are:
  - match B's withdrawal to `WithdrawalFinalized` on B's portal;
  - match B's L1 messenger `RelayedMessage` and A's L1 messenger `SentMessage(expireMessage)` in the L1 transaction that deposited into A;
  - match that deposit, by its source hash, to A's L2 transaction.
- **Check 5:** configuration drift.
- **Check 6** beyond the last-verified block: rate, lag, backlog, and stall and RPC health.
- **Check 7:** dashboards. This includes failed `expireMessage` deposits, and sends or refunds whose sender is the L2CrossDomainMessenger.
- **Overload handling.** There is no priority queue beyond refunds-first, and no backpressure.
- **Saved progress and a backfill from interop activation.** The finders still start 100 blocks back, so an event from before the monitor started is not checked. The conservation sums are rebuilt from the baseline on each start.
- **More than one RPC endpoint per chain.**
- **Devnet fault injection with broken contracts.**
- **Alert rules for `expiry_violations_total`.** They belong with the other alerting config.

## How to run

```
op-interop-mon --l2-rpcs <rpc per chain> --dependency-set <depset.json> \
  --metrics.enabled [--expiry-check-head finalized|safe] \
  [--eth-liquidity-baseline-blocks <chain-id>=<block> ...]
```

The L2 RPCs must be archive nodes back to each chain's baseline block.

Tests:

- unit tests: `go test ./op-interop-mon/...`
- acceptance test: `cd op-acceptance-tests && RUST_JIT_BUILD=1 mise exec -- just test -run TestUnrelayedMessageExpiresAndIsRefunded ./op-acceptance-tests/tests/interop/expiry/`

## Review

The `go-code-reviewer` checklist ran on this diff. Its findings are fixed, except for two that are dismissed:

- Keep `unknown_destination` as a violation. Only a chain in the source's cluster can export a fact that the source accepts, so the monitor must watch every chain in the cluster.
- The acceptance-test monitor keeps the default 7-day window instead of the system's 12 seconds. This only widens the relay search, which the destination's head bounds anyway.

The `interop-reviewer` does not apply: this is monitor-only code.

topPRs.title: op-chain-ops: add eth-liquidity-pause command
topPRs.author: karlfloersch
topPRs.body:
Stacked on #23348 (`karl/eth-liquidity-pause`). That PR makes `ETHLiquidity` mirror the chain's L1 pause through the permissionless `L1CrossDomainMessenger.syncETHLiquidityPause()`.

## What it's for

`op-chain-ops/cmd/eth-liquidity-pause` is a small CLI for the ETHLiquidity pause. It has three uses:

- **Devnet gate `interop.eth-liquidity-pause`:** `devnet-pause` → `status --expect paused` → `devnet-unpause` → `status --expect unpaused`.
- **Production verification:** `status` is read-only and works on any chain. Production pausing stays with the guardian's existing DeputyPauseModule flow, and this tool never pauses production. Nothing new is needed in superchain-ops.
- **Mirroring an L1 pause (or unpause, or expiry) to L2:** `sync` is permissionless, so any funded key can run it.

## Commands

- **`status --l2 <rpc>... [--l1 <rpc> --l1-messenger <addr>...] [--expect paused|unpaused] [--json]`**
  - For each chain it reads `ETHLiquidity.paused()` and `pausedL1Timestamp()`.
  - It runs an `eth_call` of `SuperchainETHBridge.sendETH` with 1 wei. A state override funds the dummy `--from`, so the sender needs no balance. It reports whether the call reverts and with which error (selector and name).
  - With `--l1`, it also shows `L1CrossDomainMessenger.paused()`, which is the ETHLockbox pause, and prints `OUT OF SYNC` when L1 and L2 differ.
  - `--expect` exits non-zero on any mismatch. For `paused`, every chain needs `paused()` true, `sendETH` reverting with `ETHLiquidity_Paused()` and, if read, L1 paused.
- **`sync --l1 <rpc> --l2 <rpc> --l1-messenger <addr> ... --key <any funded key>`**
  - Checks that each messenger's `SystemConfig.l2ChainId()` matches the `--l2` it is paired with.
  - Prints the L1 and L2 state per chain and skips chains already in sync (`--force` overrides).
  - Calls `syncETHLiquidityPause()`, waits for the L1 receipt, then polls L2 until `paused()` equals the L1 pause at the sync's block, or `--timeout` passes.
- **`devnet-pause` / `devnet-unpause --guardian-key <key>`**
  - Resolves each chain's ETHLockbox identifier through messenger → SystemConfig → portal → lockbox. Chains that share a lockbox are handled once.
  - Checks that the key is the SuperchainConfig guardian.
  - Calls `pause`, `extend` (if an earlier pause expired) or `unpause` on the lockbox identifier, then runs `sync`.
  - `devnet-unpause` warns if a global pause is still active.
  - Refuses OP Mainnet, Ink, Unichain, their Sepolia chains (10, 57073, 130, 11155420, 763373, 1301) and an L1 of Ethereum mainnet. There is no override flag.

Every flag can also come from `--config <toml>` (see `config.example.toml`). Local `*.toml` files in that directory are gitignored because they may hold keys.

## Usage

```bash
# Production / any chain: read-only
go run ./op-chain-ops/cmd/eth-liquidity-pause status \
  --l2 https://mainnet.optimism.io --l2 <ink-rpc> --l2 <unichain-rpc> \
  --l1 <eth-rpc> --l1-messenger <op-l1cdm> --l1-messenger <ink-l1cdm> --l1-messenger <uni-l1cdm>

# Mirror the current L1 pause to L2 (permissionless)
go run ./op-chain-ops/cmd/eth-liquidity-pause sync --config pause.toml --key <funded-l1-key>

# Devnet gate
go run ./op-chain-ops/cmd/eth-liquidity-pause devnet-pause   --config devnet.toml
go run ./op-chain-ops/cmd/eth-liquidity-pause status         --config devnet.toml --expect paused
go run ./op-chain-ops/cmd/eth-liquidity-pause devnet-unpause --config devnet.toml
go run ./op-chain-ops/cmd/eth-liquidity-pause status         --config devnet.toml --expect unpaused
```

## Tests

None of these tests need a network.

- **Calldata:** encoding for `paused()`, `syncETHLiquidityPause()`, `sendETH`, and SuperchainConfig `pause`/`unpause`/`extend`/`pausable`/`paused(address)`.
- **ABI drift:** a test checks every hand-written signature and custom error against the contracts-bedrock ABI snapshots on this stack, so a rename in #23348 fails here.
- **Revert decoding:** custom errors and `Error(string)` reasons.
- **Safety checks:** production refusal, `--l2`/`--l1-messenger` pairing, grouping chains by shared lockbox, the guardian pause/extend/unpause choice, and `--expect` evaluation, including L1 paused while L2 is not synced.
- **Config loading:** TOML values load into each command, including the example config.
- **`status` end to end:** runs against in-process fake L1/L2 JSON-RPC servers. The cases are paused and synced, unpaused, out of sync, a pre-pause ETHLiquidity, a messenger paired with the wrong chain, and JSON output. The fake rejects `sendETH` without the balance override, as geth does.
- **`sync` end to end:** runs on geth simulated backends with mock contracts. The cases are skip when in sync, `--force` send and wait for L2, a reverting call never sent, and an L2 timeout.

```
go test ./op-chain-ops/cmd/eth-liquidity-pause/...   # ok
go vet ./op-chain-ops/cmd/eth-liquidity-pause/...    # clean
./linter/bin/op-golangci-lint run ./op-chain-ops/cmd/eth-liquidity-pause/...   # 0 issues
go mod tidy -diff                                    # clean
```

I also ran `status` read-only against OP Mainnet and OP Sepolia public RPCs. ETHLiquidity is not initialized there yet, and the tool reports `Error("Proxy: implementation not initialized")` for both reads.

**Not run:** `sync` and `devnet-*` against a live devnet with #23348 deployed. The guardian path (`devnet-pause`/`devnet-unpause`) has unit coverage only for its decision logic.

topPRs.title: op-reth: acknowledge indexed proof heights
topPRs.author: joshklop
topPRs.body:
Proof-history catch-up can currently acknowledge a notification target before the asynchronous engine has indexed it, while temporary parent-state unavailability is treated as successful progress and retried without delay. This keeps `FinishedHeight` at the engine's actual indexed tip and applies exponential backoff to no-progress attempts, preventing premature replay-data pruning and tight retry loops while allowing catch-up to resume automatically.

Stacked on #23046.

Closes #23105
